subject: Post-call: Structured output reliability & SDK auth next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-call: Structured output reliability & SDK auth next steps

Hi Sarah / Acme team,

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: Reliable structured output (JSON) from LLM for invoice extraction and downstream validation.
- Constraints: On-prem data residency for PII, sub-200ms median inference for small payloads, need deterministic outputs for downstream parsers.
- Interest: SDK-based integration (server-side), secure auth (prefer mTLS or short-lived tokens), routing to cheaper/reliable model variants, embeddings + reranker for search/recall.

Technical recommendations (high-level)
- Structured output: enforce a JSON schema at generation time + post-validate; prefer constrained decoding where possible.
- Auth: for Private deployment we typically recommend mTLS; for Dedicated we can use short-lived API keys + KMS rotation.
- Routing: route by latency SLO then fallback to a smaller model variant if the primary is saturated.
- Embeddings/rerank: use embeddings for recall candidate generation, then a reranker model to score and return best structured candidates to the extractor.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a representative sample of the JSON schema you want the model to produce? (or a few example outputs)
2) Are there specific compliance checks (e.g., fields that must never be hallucinated)?
3) Would you be available for a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (Marcus + Marissa from our side to join)?

I've attached a short SDK auth guide and a sample schema we typically start from; will follow up with engineering notes on validation/retry patterns.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Marissa — looping you in for the technical follow-up with Acme (see thread above). Below are the concrete engineering notes I promised; please review and advise on feasibility/estimates.

Engineering notes (recommended approach)
1) SDK setup + auth
- Provide server-side SDK snippets for Node and Python: sample mTLS setup (client certs), and an alternate flow using short-lived tokens minted by Acme KMS with Redwood token exchange.
- Include config examples for Private vs Dedicated endpoints (endpoint url, allowed CAs, and key rotation cadence).

2) Routing and model variants
- Primary: low-latency model tuned for constrained decoding (e.g., rdx-std-4k) with streaming responses.
- Fallback: smaller quantized variant (rdx-lite) if queue delay > 150ms or error rate spikes.
- Route policy: latency-first for invoice extraction; cost-aware for batch reprocessing jobs.

3) Structured output reliability (core ask)
- At generation time: use constrained generation where we can (schema-aware token constraints). For models that don't support hard constraints, use an augmented prompt that includes the canonical JSON schema and examples, and set decoding params (temperature=0, top_p=0.7, stop tokens configured).
- Post-generation: run a strict JSON schema validator (fast, deterministic). If parse fails or schema validation fails, apply a two-step retry: 1) rerun generation with stronger constraints (temperature=0, max_tokens reduced, include "Repair the JSON to match the schema:" instruction), 2) if still invalid, call a small repair model configured with the schema-guided repair prompt.
- Fallback behavior: if repair fails, return a structured error payload with fields= null and include model-diagnostics + original text; flag for human review.

4) Embeddings + reranker flow
- Use embeddings (128/768 dim depending on model) for recall; candidate set limited to top 200 for latency.
- Use a reranker model to rescore candidates (single-turn model call) and pass top N candidates to the structured extractor.

Items I’ve attached: sample_schema.json (example invoice schema), redwood_sdk_auth_guide.pdf (mTLS + token flows). Also linking a short internal doc for the retry pattern: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-sdk-auth

Action items
- Marcus: can you confirm feasibility for constrained decoding + the repair-model pattern and estimate an engineering spike (sample code + test harness)? Rough timeline request: small POC + example <= 2 business days?
- Marissa: can you prep an estimated commercial note for Dedicated vs Private for this pilot (monthly baseline + expected token/embedding usage) to share with Acme before the deep-dive?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive for Tue/Wed based on your availability.

Best,
Rachel

Sounds good — quick notes: 
- Constrained decoding: feasible for the models we host that support token-level constraints. For others, the prompt + temperature=0 + stop tokens approach works but will need careful test vectors.
- Repair model: we have a lightweight schema-repair model (rdx-repair-small) that can be used; integrating it as a second pass should be straightforward.
- Estimate: I can build a sample Node + Python snippet with schema validation and a repair-run in ~2 business days (includes tests against the sample corpus Sarah will send).
- Embeddings/rerank: recommend 768-dim for better semantic fidelity and limit candidates to 150 for <200ms latency on Dedicated. We'll include sample benchmark numbers in the POC.

I'll start the POC tomorrow and loop in infra if we need Private endpoint certs for an mTLS demo.

—Marcus
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
